claims.claim: Reviewers note that later chapters encounter bugs and technical issues that break immersion.

citations.review_text:
as someone who originally passed this game off as a cheap cash grab due to the additional chapters all being paid DLC & originally just thinking of it as a FNAF knock-off where you can move around i see that it is so much more than that! 

The lore of this game is extremely intersting, the actual gameplay is fun and not repetitive. The chapters always contain new stuff for the player to experiment with which keeps things new and fresh.

my only gripes with the game are that certain chapters (3 & 4) can be pretty glitchy at certain points, breaking immersion. 
sometimes it just feels like a chase simulator, and rather than puzzles making sense theyre just thrown in the game to make it run a little longer- sometimes its not very clear 
BUT despite that criticism, the gameplay and lore more than makes up for a bug here or there. 

i rate this game a solid 7.5/10
with room to improve, of course- but for what it is, it's a very good experience.

(CHAPTER 5 IS THE LATEST CHAPTER OUT AT THE TIME OF THIS REVIEW!)

I like it when horror games give me a jump. Chapters 1-3 did that pretty well. But past that the game just becomes gory and buggy. Not much that actually scares me.
Later chapters are also super buggy, stiff, and they drag the story out as if to have over 8 chapters. 
A Tangible example of this is the swinging mechanic between chapters 3 and 4. It becomes super scripted and unfun to use. There is no real motion and it becomes more of a brief cutscene. All story, no gameplay.
Just watch a Youtuber at this point

Poppy playtime has to be the most BEST HORROR GAME ever made. after finally playing all the poppy playtime chapters it was so incredibly good. There are not enough words in the dictionary to describe how good this game is. in my opinion chapter 1, 2, 3, and 5 are the best chapters. and I just love this game, the mechanics the Grabpack the hands. everything. if I had to choose between FNAF and poppy playtime its going to be be POPPY Playtime. orverall 10/10.

Poppy Playtime is honestly pretty damn creepy. The whole setup takes place in an abandoned toy factory, and the game does a great job making you feel completely isolated and on edge the entire time.

The main mechanic is the Grab Pack, which gives you two long, shootable hands. You use them to grab items from far away, open doors, and route electricity to power up different rooms. The puzzles are decent, though a few sections feel a bit tedious when you are just trying to figure out where the game wants you to attach a wire next.

Where the game actually shines is the horror. Huggy Wuggy is genuinely terrifying when he starts chasing you. The vents sequence is pure panic, especially with the sound design turning up the pressure while you are scrambling to escape. It nails that specific type of mascot horror where things that should be innocent look completely warped.

The main issue is just how short it is. You can finish the first chapter in less than an hour, so it feels more like a proof of concept than a full game. It definitely leaves you wanting more, but it is a solid, quick horror experience if you want a good scare. And although the later chapters definitely play a big role, this is a good introduction into what players can expect from the franchise.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as involving puzzle-solving and exploration of the environment.

citations.review_text:
What is there to be said about this game? Poppy Playtime is a rollercoaster of an experience - it is frankly impossible to describe, and to the general audience, they might not even believe me if I told them what this game was really about. Yet, while many people seem to be dead set on this game being complete garbage, what you'll actually find in Poppy Playtime is an admittedly inconsistent and flawed, yet extremely fascinating game, slowly weaving a deeply disturbing yet beautiful tale, and brimming with interesting scares, mechanics, and characters that more often than not make a game that ultimately deserves to be the phenomenon that it is. 

Let me make one thing clear, though - this game is not for everyone, and there are a lot of things in this game that could very well turn someone off. At its core, this game is a puzzle/horror game with mild stealth elements. If you do not like story games and/or doing lots and lots of puzzle solving, you will not enjoy this game. If you do not like exploration, finding scraps of story hidden around the environment and piecing together a larger narrative, you will not like this game. Despite its inherent mass appeal, this game is not built for everyone, and its important to set some expectations if you decide to give it a try.

That also being said, the game itself is imperfect. Extreme inconsistencies between chapters, both graphically and technically, and a struggle to balance all of its moving parts and elements permeate the entire experience. There is a very clear point in the game where development conditions shifted drastically, resulting in a major narrative seam. On top of all of this, there are many moments where the puzzles do not land, characters and ideas that go extremely underdeveloped, and moments of potentially frustrating game design that might make you wonder why I'd ever recommend this to anyone!

The truth is, I recommend this game because I believe that there is something truly special to be found…

citations.review_text:
Poppy Playtime is a creepy, fun little horror game with a great atmosphere. Exploring the abandoned toy factory is genuinely unsettling, and the GrabPack puzzles add a clever twist to the usual hide-and-seek gameplay. Huggy Wuggy is an instantly memorable monster, and the game does a nice job building suspense as you uncover what happened at Playtime Co.

It’s fairly short, and some sections can feel a bit simple, but the setting and scares make it worth playing—especially if you enjoy puzzle-based horror.

I will review each chapter on their steam page, this is the first one. I think this is a good introduction to the game, and I can see this being scary as well. This is quite short though, it's more like a demo for the other chapters. Poppy Playtime is a puzzle game, so expect there to be a lot of puzzles throughout all the chapters. If you don't like puzzles, then this isn't the game for you. This chapter has one of the best chase scenes of these chapters, so that's a good thing. Chapter 1 has the weakest story of all of them, but that leaves a lot of mystery for the other chapters to solve. Overall, it is a good introduction and you should definitely play it. Especially since it's free. Then if you enjoyed this, you can get the other chapters. They get better than this one.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the GrabPack hands solve puzzles for you.

citation.review_text:
Don't usually review games on Steam, but I'll make an acceptation for Poppy. I first encountered this game a little after the first chapter's release, through my little brother of course, and brainrot youtube videos that led me to believe this game was something entirely different from what it really is. Once I played it at some point, a little before the second chapter was published, I instantly fell in love with it.
Chapter 1 is a great introduction. Great mechanics with the GrabPack hands, Poppy Playtime's saving grace---the fun, gummy hands that solve puzzles for you! Cool concept, little hints that pay off later in the series, through posters and VHS tapes, and a terrifying antagonist by the equally terrifying name... Huggy Wuggy... 
His vent chase is by far the best chase sequence in the series, maybe even topping a specific sequence toward the end of the latest chapter. 
Overall, great demo! Glad it's free now.
